mainTopic: Whether a זר is liable for arranging the wood on the מזבח (the מערכה or the two logs), and the related rules of daytime service and the פייס.
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier derivation: the verse refers to the טלה of the morning תמיד. Then רבי יוחנן rules that a זר who arranges the wood pile (מערכה) on the מזבח is חייב, and that a כהן must rebuild the pile. רבי זירא objects that arranging the pile may be done at night, so it cannot be a real עבודה reserved for כהנים. The גמרא tests his rule with the burning of אברים ופדרים and with תרומת הדשן. It answers that these count as the end and the start of the daytime service, so his objection stands. רבי יוחנן's statement is therefore reworded: a זר is liable for placing the שני גזירי עצים, since that is a daytime service. רבא asks why that service has no פייס. The גמרא answers that it is included in the lottery for תרומת הדשן, and then explains the exceptions to the lottery rules. מר זוטרא challenges the claim that the logs belong to the daytime from a משנה, and the גמרא answers him. Finally, another version of רבי זירא's objection is brought: arranging the pile is followed by another service, so a זר should not be liable for it. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse refers to the lamb of the morning offering
steps.stepSummary: The earlier derivation ends: the offering hinted at in the verse is the טלה of the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say that this is the lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an argument that started on the previous page. It decides that the offering the verse is talking about is the טלה of the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא had been testing which offering the verse could mean and ruling out the other options. With 'הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר', it closes the elimination: only the morning תמיד lamb fits. This lets the verse teach how the תמיד is brought.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say / it must be (concludes an elimination)
Lamb (here, the lamb of the תמיד)

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the previous discussion. The new topic (a זר arranging the wood) only starts in the next step.

phrases.english: You must say: this is the lamb.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the proof that started on the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes a derivation begun on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The verse refers to the טלה of the morning תמיד.

steps.title: A non-priest who arranged the wood pile is liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a זר who arranged the מערכה is חייב. He adds that the pile must be taken apart and rebuilt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A non-priest who arranged the wood pile is liable. What does he do? He takes it apart and arranges it again.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן says that arranging the wood on the מזבח counts as a real עבודה, so a זר who does it is punished. He also explains how to fix the pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the זר חייב (מיתה בידי שמים) shows that סידור המערכה counts as a full עבודה reserved for כהנים. Since the זר's arrangement is invalid, the pile has to be dismantled and set up again. The wording 'he dismantles it and rearranges it' sounds as if the same זר rebuilds it, and the next step will question that.

keyTerms.meaning: The arranged wood pile on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the sugya: does arranging the wood count as a real עבודה?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A non-priest who arranged the wood pile
is liable.
How does he proceed (to fix it)?
He dismantles it and arranges it again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous derivation ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר who arranges the מערכה is חייב. The pile must be dismantled and rearranged.

steps.title: What would rebuilding by the same person accomplish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what good it does if the same זר rebuilds the pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would that help?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the fix in step 2. If the זר rebuilds the pile himself, it is just as invalid as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with the first pile was that a זר arranged it. Taking it apart and having the same זר build it again changes nothing. So the wording of the fix cannot mean what it seems to say.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it help? / What is accomplished?

phrases.english: What good does it do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the fix described in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rebuild done by the same זר has the same flaw as the first pile, so it fixes nothing.

steps.title: The non-priest dismantles, a priest rearranges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the fix: the זר may take the pile apart, but a כהן must rebuild it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: a non-priest dismantles it, and a priest arranges it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading the fix. Two different people are involved: a זר takes it apart and a כהן puts it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dismantling is not an עבודה, so a זר may do it. Arranging the wood is an עבודה, so only a כהן may do it. This keeps רבי יוחנן's ruling intact and makes the fix actually work.

phrases.english: Rather:
a non-priest dismantles it,
and a priest arranges it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of the wording (who does each action)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same זר dismantles and rebuilds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זר dismantles and a כהן rebuilds.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, arranging the wood is a כהן-only עבודה. Taking it apart may be done by anyone.

steps.title: A service valid at night cannot be forbidden to a non-priest
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects: a service valid at night is not a real עבודה, so it should be permitted to a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Is there any service that is valid at night and yet invalid when done by a non-priest?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רבי יוחנן's whole ruling from step 2. He argues that something valid at night cannot be a real עבודה reserved for כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real עבודה in the מקדש is done by day. The מערכה may be arranged at night, which shows it is not a full עבודה. If it is not a full עבודה, a זר should be allowed to do it, and he should not be חייב.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not questioning the wood-pile fix. He is challenging the basic idea that a זר is חייב for arranging the wood at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected to it:
Is there any service
that is valid at night
and invalid by a non-priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the core ruling of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a זר who arranges the מערכה is חייב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only daytime acts are real עבודה. The מערכה may be arranged at night, so it is not a real עבודה and should not be forbidden to a זר.

steps.title: Burning limbs and fats is a counterexample
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא: burning אברים ופדרים happens at night, yet a זר is forbidden to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there not? But what about the limbs and fats?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רבי זירא's rule by offering a counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning of אברים ופדרים on the מזבח goes on all night, and earlier in the פרק a זר who does it is חייב מיתה. That looks like exactly the kind of case רבי זירא said does not exist.

phrases.english: And is there not?
But what about the limbs and fats?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's general rule from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that no night-valid service is forbidden to a זר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning אברים ופדרים is valid at night and still forbidden to a זר, which contradicts his rule.

steps.title: Night burning is the end of a daytime service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבי זירא: burning limbs at night is only the finish of a service that began by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the end of a daytime service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the counterexample and keeps רבי זירא's rule standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning of אברים ופדרים is not a separate night service. It completes the sacrifice that was offered during the day. So it is really part of daytime עבודה, and רבי זירא's rule still holds for true night services like arranging the wood.

phrases.english: It is the end of a daytime service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the counterexample of step 6 in defense of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the counterexample (it belongs to the daytime service)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning limbs is a night service forbidden to a זר.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the conclusion of a daytime service, so it does not contradict רבי זירא.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's challenge to רבי יוחנן still stands for now: a truly nighttime act like arranging the wood seems not to be a full עבודה. Step 11 resolves this by rewording רבי יוחנן's statement.

steps.title: What about removing the ashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא with תרומת הדשן, which is done at night yet is forbidden to a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the removal of the ashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case against רבי זירא's rule. Removing the ashes is done at night, but a זר may not do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said a service done at night is not a real עבודה, so a זר should be allowed to do it. תרומת הדשן is done before dawn and is still forbidden to a זר. That seems to break his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a portion of ashes from the altar, done before dawn
But look at this case (introduces a counter-example)

phrases.english: But what about the removal of the ashes!
phrases.notes: That job was done at night, yet a זר still isn't allowed to do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new counter-example after the limbs case was answered in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule that a night service is not a real עבודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומת הדשן is done at night, yet a זר is forbidden to do it

steps.title: Removing the ashes begins the daytime service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תרומת הדשן is the start of the day's service. It proves this from רבי יוחנן's ruling about washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the start of the daytime service. As רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a כהן washed his hands for the removal of the ashes, he does not need to wash again the next morning, since he already washed at the start of the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא. Removing the ashes is not a separate night service; it is the beginning of the day's work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the washing of the hands. Washing for תרומת הדשן counts for the whole next day's service. That shows the ash removal belongs to the following day, not to the night.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctified, meaning washed, his hands (and feet) from the כיור

phrases.english: It is the beginning of the daytime service.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he sanctified his hands for the removal of the ashes,
the next day he does not need to sanctify again,
since he already sanctified at the start of the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the case as part of the daytime service
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומת הדשן is a night service that is still forbidden to a זר
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the start of the daytime service, so רבי זירא's rule stands

steps.title: So the challenge against רבי יוחנן stands
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי זירא's rule survived every test, his objection to רבי יוחנן's statement stands. The next step resolves it by rewording רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי זירא's objection to רבי יוחנן is still standing. This also sets up the rewriting of רבי יוחנן's statement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's rule held up against both the limbs and the ashes. That means his original objection remains. Arranging the pile is a night service, so it should be permitted to a זר, and רבי יוחנן's ruling seems wrong.

phrases.english: If so, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: So רבי זירא's question on רבי יוחנן still stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of steps 6 through 9
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא's objection to רבי יוחנן's original statement stands. Step 11 resolves it by rewording the statement.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's statement is rewritten: the two logs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises רבי יוחנן's statement. A זר is liable for placing the שני גזירי עצים, because that is a daytime service.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is how it was said: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a זר who arranged the two logs is liable, since it is a daytime service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the wording of רבי יוחנן's statement so that it no longer conflicts with רבי זירא. It is now about the two logs placed during the day, not the night arrangement of the pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing the two logs happens in the daytime. Under רבי זירא's rule, that makes it a real עבודה. So a זר who does it is liable to death by the hand of Heaven, and the conflict disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: When it was said, this is how it was said (introduces a corrected version)
The two logs placed on the altar with the morning תמיד

steps.whyThisMatters: This revised statement becomes the foundation for רבא's objection and the whole discussion of פייס that follows.

phrases.english: Rather, when it was stated, this is how it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: זָר שֶׁסִּידֵּר שְׁנֵי גְּזִירֵי עֵצִים חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: A non-priest who arranged the two logs is liable,
since it is a daytime service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the standing difficulty of step 10 by changing the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן spoke about the arrangement of the pile, a night service
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן spoke about the two logs, a daytime service

steps.title: רבא: then it should need a lottery
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that if the two logs are a real daytime service, there should be a פייס for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: if so, it should require a lottery!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the revised statement. Daytime services are assigned by lottery, but we never hear of a lottery for the two logs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumes that every real daytime עבודה gets its own פייס. The משנה lists the lotteries and does not mention the two logs. So either it is not a real daytime service, or something is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, from now on
The lottery assigning Temple services to כהנים

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to it:
But if so, it should require a lottery!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה תִּיבְּעֵי פַּיִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the revised statement in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The revised statement of רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Daytime services require a פייס, yet there is no separate lottery for the two logs

steps.title: The two logs are included in the ashes lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבא forgot a ברייתא: whoever wins תרומת הדשן also does the arrangement and the two logs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא forgot what was taught: whoever won the removal of the ashes also won the arranging of the pile and the arranging of the two logs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא. There is a lottery for the two logs; it is simply bundled into the lottery for removing the ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that one פייס covers three jobs. So the two logs do get assigned by lottery, and רבא's objection falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranging the woodpile on the altar

phrases.english: It escaped him, that which is taught:
One who won the removal of the ashes,
won the arranging of the woodpile
and the arranging of the two logs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a ברייתא that רבא overlooked
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no lottery for the two logs
steps.terutzMaskana: The two logs are covered by the lottery for תרומת הדשן

steps.title: Do only daytime services need a lottery? What about the limbs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבא's assumption, citing אברים ופדרים, which are burned at night yet assigned by lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that a daytime service needs a lottery and a night service does not? But what about the limbs and fats?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבא's assumption that only daytime services get a lottery. Burning the limbs happens at night, yet it has a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's question implied a rule: day services need a פייס, night services do not. The limbs and fats are burned at night and are still assigned by lottery. That looks like a counter-example.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (tests an implied rule)
Limbs and fats of the offerings burned on the altar

phrases.english: Is that to say that a daytime service requires a lottery
and a night service does not require a lottery?
But what about the limbs and fats!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the assumption behind רבא's objection
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule that only daytime services need a פייס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Limbs and fats are burned at night but require a lottery

steps.title: Burning the limbs ends the daytime service
steps.stepSummary: The limbs and fats are the end of the daytime service, so they count as day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the end of the daytime service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same answer as step 7. Burning the limbs at night only finishes what began during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because it completes a daytime offering, it is treated as part of the day. That is why it has a lottery, and the rule still holds.

phrases.english: It is the end of the daytime service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the case as the end of a day service
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Limbs are a night service that has a lottery
steps.terutzMaskana: They are the end of a day service, so the rule holds

steps.title: What about removing the ashes, which has a lottery?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings תרומת הדשן, a night service that has its own lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the removal of the ashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another counter-example. Removing the ashes is done at night, yet it is assigned by lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is about the lottery, not about whether a זר may do it. תרומת הדשן has the first פייס, even though it happens at night.

phrases.english: But what about the removal of the ashes!
phrases.notes: These are the same words as step 8, but now the question is about the lottery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new counter-example after step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that night services do not need a פייס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומת הדשן is done at night and has a lottery

steps.title: The ashes lottery came from a past incident
steps.stepSummary: The lottery for תרומת הדשן was added because of the incident in the משנה, when כהנים raced up the ramp and one was hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the incident that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that this lottery is a special enactment. It was added because of the danger that happened when כהנים raced for the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the basic rule, תרומת הדשן would not need a lottery. The חכמים added one after a כהן was injured in the race up the ramp. So it is an exception with its own reason, not a disproof of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The incident that occurred (the race on the ramp in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two times the ashes are mentioned. In step 9 the question was whether a זר may do it. Here the question is why it has a lottery, and the answer is a historical enactment.

phrases.english: Because of the incident that occurred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: A special enactment explains the exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ashes lottery shows that night services need a פייס
steps.terutzMaskana: That lottery was added only because of the incident

steps.title: Must a lottery service also be forbidden to a זר? What about slaughtering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests a further implied rule: only daytime services forbidden to a זר need a lottery. Slaughtering is permitted to a זר, yet it has a lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that a daytime service for which a זר is liable to death needs a lottery, and one for which a זר is not liable does not? But what about slaughtering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the rule also requires the service to be forbidden to a זר. Slaughtering is valid even when a זר does it, yet it is assigned by lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא linked the lottery to the two logs, a service for which a זר is liable. That suggests a lottery only applies when a זר would be liable. שחיטה is kosher by a זר, but it is still in the פייס.

keyTerms.meaning: Death penalty (here, by the hand of Heaven)
Slaughtering the offering, which is valid even by a זר

phrases.english: Is that to say that a daytime service

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁזָּר חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִיתָה בָּעֲיָא פַּיִיס,
phrases.english: for which a non-priest is liable to death requires a lottery,
while one for which a non-priest is not liable to death
does not require a lottery?
But what about slaughtering!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדַת יוֹם וְשֶׁזָּר חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִיתָה בָּעֲיָא פַּיִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a second assumption behind רבא's objection
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule that only services forbidden to a זר need a פייס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שחיטה is permitted to a זר yet is assigned by lottery

steps.title: Slaughtering is different: it begins the service
steps.stepSummary: שחיטה gets a lottery because it is the beginning of the offering's service.
steps.simpleTranslation: Slaughtering is different, because it is the beginning of the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that slaughtering is a special case. It opens the whole service of the offering, so it is important enough for a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though a זר may slaughter, שחיטה starts the entire process of the קרבן. That importance earns it a place in the פייס, and the general rule stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: A night service is not a real עבודה unless it is the start or the end of a day service. The revised רבי יוחנן says a זר is liable for the two logs, which are covered by the ashes lottery. Each exception to the lottery rules has a reason: the limbs end a day service, the ashes lottery came from an incident, and שחיטה begins the service.

phrases.english: Slaughtering is different, for it is the beginning of the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case by its importance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שחיטה shows the rule about a זר's liability is wrong
steps.terutzMaskana: שחיטה is an exception because it begins the service

steps.title: The משנה checks the time for slaughtering, not for the logs
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא (or רב אשי) challenges רבי יוחנן's revised statement. The משנה only tells the כהנים to check whether it is time for שחיטה. It never tells them to check whether it is time for the two logs.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said, and some say רב אשי: But didn't we learn otherwise in the משנה? There the appointed officer said to them, 'Go out and see whether the time for slaughtering has arrived.' Yet it does not say 'the time of the two logs.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא brings a משנה to argue against the idea that arranging the two logs must wait for daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the morning service, the ממונה sent someone to check whether daylight had come. He asked only about שחיטה. If the logs also had to wait for day, the משנה should have said 'see if the time for the logs has come.' Its silence suggests the logs could be arranged while it was still night.

keyTerms.meaning: The appointed officer in charge of the כהנים' duties
The two logs of wood added to the altar fire each morning
'It does not teach': points out what a source leaves out

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Mar Zutra said, and some say Rav Ashi:
But didn't we learn that it is not so?
phrases.notes: Opens a challenge from a משנה.

phrases.english: The appointed officer said to them:

phrases.aramaic: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ אִם הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטָה.
phrases.english: Go out and see if the time for slaughtering has arrived.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ ״זְמַן שְׁנֵי גְּזִירֵי עֵצִים״ לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: Whereas 'the time of the two logs' it does not teach.
phrases.notes: Since it doesn't mention the logs, that suggests they could be arranged at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רבי יוחנן's revised statement, which treats arranging the two logs as daytime service.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that arranging the two logs is a daytime service
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה checks for daylight only for שחיטה. Leaving out the logs implies they need not wait for day.

steps.title: The משנה mentions only what cannot be fixed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה names שחיטה because slaughtering at night cannot be corrected. Logs arranged too early can simply be removed and placed again.
steps.simpleTranslation: That which has no remedy, it teaches. That which has a remedy, it does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by explaining why the משנה mentions only שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal slaughtered before daybreak becomes permanently invalid, so the משנה stresses checking the time for it. Logs placed too early can be taken off and put back properly, so there was no need to mention them. The logs still belong in the daytime. The משנה simply focused on the case where a mistake is permanent.

keyTerms.meaning: A remedy or way to fix a mistake
'That one': points to a particular case

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say the logs may be arranged at night. They still belong in the daytime. The משנה just did not bother to mention them, because an early placement can be redone.

phrases.english: That which has no remedy, it teaches,
phrases.notes: Slaughtering at night is permanently invalid.

phrases.aramaic: הָךְ דְּאִית לַהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא — לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: That which has a remedy, it does not teach.
phrases.notes: Logs can be removed and arranged again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 by explaining why the משנה leaves out the logs.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's wording: it names only the case that cannot be fixed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the משנה does not mention the logs, they could be arranged at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: The logs are still daytime service. The משנה mentioned שחיטה only because a mistake there is permanent.

steps.title: Another version: no service followed by more service makes a non-priest liable
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי זירא objects to רבי יוחנן's original ruling that a זר who arranges the מערכה is liable. Arranging the wood pile is followed by another service, placing the שני גזירי עצים, and a זר is liable only for a service that completes the task.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: רבי זירא objected strongly. Do you have any service that is followed by another service and is still forbidden to a זר, making him liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבי זירא's objection to רבי יוחנן's original ruling in step 2, that a זר who arranges the wood pile is liable. In this version the problem is not that the act is done at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק we learned a rule: a זר is liable only for a complete service, one that is not followed by another service that finishes the job. Arranging the wood pile is followed by another service, placing the שני גזירי עצים. By that rule, a זר should not be liable for arranging the pile.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Objects strongly to it': introduces a forceful challenge
A service followed by further service, so it is not complete on its own
Invalid when done by a non-כהן, making him liable

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects to the rule of עבודה תמה, a complete service. That rule decides when a זר is liable for doing a Temple service.

phrases.english: And some say:
phrases.notes: Here comes another version of the question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objected to it:
And do you have any service
that is followed by another service
and is invalid when done by a non-priest?
phrases.notes: Meaning: a זר who does it would be liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a different version of רבי זירא's objection (compare step 5) to רבי יוחנן's original statement in step 2. It is based on 'a service followed by another service' instead of 'valid at night'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's original ruling (step 2) that a זר who arranges the מערכה is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זר is liable only for a complete service. Arranging the wood pile is followed by placing the two logs, so it should not make a זר liable.
